decisions.reason: As a standard handle family in the core assortment, it remains inexpensive to carry and still offers option value, though after another year without standout signals the withdrawal risk rises slightly.

The mitred family broadens the architectural design offer and is still worth keeping as a low-cost option, but by 2025 its market acceptance should be clearer so the risk of pruning is moderately higher.

Its multifunctional and more specialized character makes it the weakest of the remaining options, yet it still fits the firm's accessibility and system-solution direction well enough to justify staying on the market for now.
This handle line stays close to established manufacturing, certification and sales capabilities, so the cost of continuation is low and real-options logic still favors keeping it.
The dedicated launch treatment and design-award signal suggest durable strategic and reputational value, making withdrawal within the next year unlikely.
